Rules / Correctness

SK2180 The foreach casts every element down to a narrower type

The loop variable's type is narrower than the sequence's element type, so the language inserts a cast the source does not show and the loop throws on the first element that is not of that type.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

foreach (Derived d in items) over an IEnumerable<Base> is not a filter and not a check: C# writes an explicit conversion into the loop for you, and the loop stops with an InvalidCastException on the first element that is something else. The cast is the one operation in C# that a foreach performs and does not spell — var shows nothing, the declared type reads as documentation, and every review of the line reads it as the element type rather than as an assertion about it. ⚠ This is the part of issue #2 that is neither a compiler diagnostic nor a value-lattice problem. The impossible conversions in that issue are CS0030 — probed at AnalysisMode=All, (Sealed)derived, (IUnrelated)sealedValue and (Sealed)unrelatedInterface are all errors, so that code never reaches a linter. What is left of the issue after the compiler has taken its share is a downcast that is possible and unannounced, and only the foreach form is decidable without reasoning about which values reach the site.

Example

Instead of:

void M(List<Shape> shapes) {
    foreach (Circle c in shapes) {
        Draw(c);
    }
}

Write:

void M(List<Shape> shapes) {
    foreach (var c in shapes.OfType<Circle>()) {
        Draw(c);
    }
}

When it does not fire

⚠ A sequence whose element type is `object` is never reported, and that exclusion carries most of the rule's safety. foreach (string s in arrayList) over a non-generic IEnumerable, an ArrayList or a List<object> has no other spelling: the cast is what the language offers for a sequence that is untyped by construction, and reporting it would be telling the author to stop using an API they do not control. What is reported is the case where the sequence is typed and the loop narrows it anyway, which is where a typed collection or an OfType was available and was not used. ⚠ Only reference conversions and unboxings. A narrowing numeric conversion in a foreach — foreach (int i in longs) — cannot throw outside a checked context and is a different concept; ClassifyConversion decides this, and only IsReference or IsUnboxing reaches a report. Type parameters, dynamic and error types are declined outright, for SK2121's reason: inside a generic method the conversion is classified against the constraint set rather than against the instantiated type. An identity or widening loop variable — foreach (Base b in derivedItems) — is not a downcast and is silent. ⚠ Report-only, deliberately. The two rewrites are OfType<T>(), which skips the elements that do not match, and an explicit cast in the body, which still throws — the source says which behaviour it has and does not say which behaviour was wanted, so an automatic edit would have to guess between silently dropping data and keeping the exception. Generated code is excluded.
